getaway_note: Cassini's getaway burn (ESA: 28 December, about 24 m/s), timed from the reconstructed trajectory: a 23.8 m/s step between 23:30 and 00:00 UTC. Without the probe's own track, ESA's separation numbers place it until then.

facts.text: Huygens separated from Cassini on 25 December 2004 at 02:00 UTC.
Cassini switched to coast mode, with its RCS thrusters inhibited, 10 seconds before separation; they were re-enabled about 60 seconds after.
The Spin/Eject Device released Huygens at about 0.35 m/s relative speed and a spin of 7.5 rpm; the whole release took about 0.15 seconds.
Pyrotechnic devices fired, then push-off springs, ramps and rollers moved the probe away from the orbiter.
The probe weighs 320 kg; the two spacecraft together weighed 5548 kg at launch.
Cassini's magnetometer saw the probe's spin and confirmed 7.5 revolutions per minute, the rate predicted.
There was no contact with Earth during the release; Cassini recorded it, then turned to Earth, and the signal took 1 hour 8 minutes to arrive from 1.2 billion km away.
The probe coasted, dormant, for 20 days; its timer started it up about 5 hours before it reached the entry altitude of 1270 km above Titan.
On 28 December 2004 Cassini made a deflection manoeuvre of about 24 m/s so it would fly past Titan at 60,000 km instead of following the probe.
Huygens entered Titan's atmosphere on 14 January 2005 at about 09:06 UTC, at about 6 km/s and a steep 65 degrees.
